items.title: Chinese scientists turn CO2 into petrol components using solar power

featured_image.name: How Chinese scientists made petrol building blocks with CO2, water and sunlight

items.description:
Chinese researchers have developed a solar-powered method to convert carbon dioxide and water into chemicals that can serve as building blocks for petrol, mimicking the natural process of photosynthesis found in plants. The breakthrough could offer a more sustainable pathway to produce fuel for sectors that are difficult to electrify, such as aviation and shipping.

The team from the Chinese Academy of Sciences and the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology published their findings in the peer-reviewed journal Nature Communications last week. Drawing inspiration from how plants convert sunlight, CO2, and water into energy, the researchers created a specialized material that stores small amounts of electrical energy to efficiently drive chemical reactions.[1][2][3][4]

items.title: IAEA warns of nuclear risk after Russian strikes halt Ukraine plants

featured_image.name: IAEA chief warns of nuclear risk from Russia attacks on Ukraine power grids

items.description:
A massive Russian missile and drone attack struck Ukraine's energy infrastructure on February 7, forcing all nuclear power plants in Kyiv-controlled territory to halt electricity generation and prompting the International Atomic Energy Agency to issue urgent warnings about growing threats to nuclear safety.

IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi called for military restraint after the strikes damaged key high-voltage substations that supply power to nuclear facilities, describing the deteriorating grid situation as compromising nuclear safety with potentially dangerous repercussions.[1][2][3]

items.title: SpaceX begins hiring for Musk's million-satellite data center plan

featured_image.name: SpaceX asks FCC to approve 1 million solar-powered AI data ...

items.description:
Elon Musk is moving forward with an audacious plan to build artificial intelligence data centers in space, with SpaceX now actively recruiting engineers for the project despite widespread skepticism from industry experts about its technical feasibility.

SpaceX filed an application with the Federal Communications Commission on January 30, 2026, seeking approval to launch up to one million satellites designed to operate as orbital data centers powered by near-constant solar energy. The company argues the system would "achieve transformative cost and energy efficiency while significantly reducing the environmental impact associated with terrestrial data centers."[1][2]

items.title: Zelensky warns against $12 trillion Russia-US deal without Kyiv

featured_image.name: Zelensky alleges Russian plan to attack Ukraine's nuclear ...

items.description:
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky on Saturday voiced strong opposition to a proposed $12 trillion economic cooperation package between Russia and the United States, warning that any bilateral agreement affecting Ukraine without Kyiv's participation would be unacceptable.

Speaking to journalists in Kyiv on February 6, with comments embargoed until Saturday, Zelensky revealed that Ukrainian intelligence services had briefed him on what he termed the "Dmitriev package," named after Russian negotiator Kirill Dmitriev, who heads the state-controlled Russian Direct Investment Fund.[1][2]

"Intelligence showed me the so-called 'Dmitriev package' that he presented in the U.S. — it amounts to around $12 trillion," Zelensky said, describing it as a proposed framework for large-scale economic cooperation between Washington and Moscow.[3][1]

items.title: Iran's foreign minister warns of strikes on US bases if attacked

featured_image.name: Iran threatens to strike US bases if conflict erupts over nuclear programme

items.description:
Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi issued a warning on Saturday that Tehran would target American military installations across the Middle East if the United States launches an attack on the Islamic Republic, while emphasizing such strikes should not be interpreted as aggression toward the host nations.[1][2][3]

"It would not be possible to attack American soil, but we will target their bases in the region," Araghchi told Qatari Al Jazeera television. "We will not attack neighboring countries; rather, we will target U.S. bases stationed in them. There is a big difference between the two."[2][4][3][1]

The warning comes amid heightened tensions as the Trump administration maintains a substantial naval presence in the region, with the USS Abraham Lincoln carrier strike group positioned in the Arabian Sea alongside additional warships equipped with Tomahawk missiles. President Donald Trump has referred to the deployment as a "massive armada" while warning of potential military action should Iran refuse to negotiate on its nuclear program.[5][6][7][8]

items.title: Netanyahu to meet Trump Wednesday to discuss US-Iran talks

featured_image.name: Israel’s Netanyahu to meet with Trump at White House next week

items.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu will travel to Washington on Wednesday to discuss ongoing US-Iran nuclear negotiations with President Donald Trump, his office announced Saturday. The visit represents an acceleration of diplomatic coordination as high-stakes talks between Washington and Tehran appear to be gaining momentum.

The meeting comes just days after the first round of indirect nuclear talks between US and Iranian officials concluded in Muscat, Oman, on Friday. Both sides described the discussions as constructive and agreed to continue negotiations, though substantial gaps remain on key issues.

items.title: Trump lifts India tariffs, threatens levies on Iran trade partners

featured_image.name: Trump Announces Trade Deal With India to Reduce Tariffs

items.description:
President Donald Trump signed two executive orders Friday reshaping American trade policy across multiple fronts, rolling back punitive tariffs on India following New Delhi's commitment to halt Russian oil imports while simultaneously threatening duties on nations that continue to trade with Iran.

The dual moves underscore the Trump administration's use of tariffs as a lever in negotiations involving both allies and adversaries, with implications stretching from the Indo-Pacific to the Middle East.

items.title: China launches reusable spaceplane for fourth orbital mission

featured_image.name: China launches reusable spacecraft for fourth time since 2020

items.description:
China successfully sent a reusable experimental spacecraft into orbit on Saturday, marking the fourth mission for the shadowy vehicle since 2020. The launch took place at the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in the Gobi Desert, northwest China, using a Long March-2F carrier rocket.[1][2][3]

The spacecraft lifted off between 11:48 a.m. and 12:07 p.m. China Standard Time, according to the space tracking site China-in-Space. State news agency Xinhua reported that the experimental spacecraft "will conduct planned technical verification of reusable spacecraft technology, providing technical support for the peaceful use of space."[2][4][5]

items.title: Chinese researchers achieve perovskite solar cell breakthrough

featured_image.name: Perovskite solar cells boosted to 26% power with over 1,000 ...

items.description:
Separate research teams in China and Europe have pushed perovskite solar cell efficiency beyond 26 percent using new chemical and interface engineering approaches, marking a milestone in the race to commercialize this promising photovoltaic technology.

The advances address one of the central challenges facing perovskite solar cells: reconciling high efficiency with long-term stability under sunlight. While these cells have emerged as a low-cost alternative to silicon-based panels, their tendency to degrade when exposed to light and oxygen has hindered commercial deployment.
